scope: Proposition 4.7 (Cross-layer charge count) of the manuscript “The Boltzmann–Grad limit for stable radial potentials on regular kinetic intervals” (preprints/The-Boltzmann-Grad-limit-for-stable-radial-potentials-on-regular-kinetic-intervals-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 364 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce9fe5976f17b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider a term remaining after Proposition 4.5, with no unresolved cutoff interruption. Let H count the root slots entering each expanded layer at its upper cut, including the starting roots and residual slots, summed over those layers. Retained inputs at time zero are terminal charges, not additional root occurrences in H. Let h0 count uncentered restarting top roots, let d be the number of distinct marked lives, let r be the number of residual factors, and let i be the number of retained singleton factors at time zero. With at most L expanded layers, H ≤ Lh0 + L2 d + Lr + Li. (4.23) In particular, if H ≥ δp and h0 ≤ δp/(2L), then d + r + i ≥ δ 2L2 p. (4.24) The statement is purely combinatorial and imposes no smallness on an uncentered restarting top.
